operations.description:
Update an administrator promotion request by reviewing and deciding on it.

Super administrators use this endpoint to approve or reject administrator promotion requests submitted by members or sellers. When approving, the applicant becomes a regular administrator. When rejecting, a rejection note should be provided to explain the decision.

The request status can only be updated from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected'. Once a decision is made, the request cannot be modified further. The reviewing super administrator's ID is automatically recorded.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate that the requesting user is a super administrator by checking session and grade level. Load the promotion request by UUID from shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests table. Verify the request status is 'pending' - reject if already approved or rejected. Validate the request body: status must be 'approved' or 'rejected', and if 'rejected', rejection_note must be provided and non-empty. Update the status field, set rejection_note if provided, and set reviewed_by_super_admin_id to the current super administrator's ID. If status is 'approved', create a record in shopping_mall_administrators table: link to the applicant's member ID (from subtype table), set grade to 'regular'. Use transaction to ensure atomicity. Return the updated promotion request with all fields including reviewer ID, rejection note, and updated timestamps.

responseBody.description: The updated administrator promotion request with the decision applied, including reviewer information, rejection note if rejected, and updated timestamps.

parameters.description: UUID of the administrator promotion request to review (global scope).
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: Update data including the decision status (approved or rejected) and optional rejection note explaining the decision when rejected.

prerequisites.description: Member must submit a promotion request before a super administrator can review and update it
Seller must submit a promotion request before a super administrator can review and update it

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of categories with optional filtering and search capabilities.

This endpoint returns all categories in the system, supporting filtering by parent category to retrieve subcategories, text search by category name, and pagination for large result sets. Categories are organized in a two-tier hierarchy where top-level categories have no parent and subcategories belong to exactly one parent category.

Customers can browse all categories to explore products. Administrators use this endpoint to manage the category catalog. When viewing a parent category, customers see all products in that category and its subcategories. Subcategories cannot have their own subcategories, enforcing one level of nesting only.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_categories table with pagination support. Apply filters based on request criteria: parentId for subcategory filtering, search term for name matching using LIKE operator. Sort by display order or creation date. Join with product count aggregation if requested. Return cursor-based or offset pagination with category summary objects including id, name, description, parentId, and product count. Handle empty result sets gracefully.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of category summary records with hierarchical structure information and optional product counts for administrative and customer browsing displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including parent category ID filter for subcategory retrieval, text search for category name matching, and pagination parameters for result set navigation.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific category by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete category record including the category name, description, parent category reference (if this is a subcategory), and timestamps. Customers can use this to view category details when browsing the product catalog. Administrators can use this to view category information before editing or managing the category.

The category hierarchy is limited to one level of nesting. If the parent_id field is populated, this category is a subcategory of the referenced parent category. If parent_id is null, this is a top-level category. Products assigned to this category will be visible when customers browse this category or its parent category (if applicable).
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_categories table by the provided categoryId UUID parameter.

Retrieve the complete category record including: id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

If parent_id is not null, optionally join with the parent category to include parent category details in the response for client convenience.

Return 404 error if the category does not exist or has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null).

No authentication required for basic category viewing - accessible to guest, customer, seller, and admin actors.

responseBody.description: Complete category entity including hierarchical relationship to parent category and metadata timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the category to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: categoryId

operations.description:
Retrieves all subcategories (direct children) under a specific parent category.

This endpoint returns the immediate child categories of the specified parent category, enabling hierarchical category browsing. Only one level of nesting is supported per business rules - subcategories cannot have their own children.

The response includes category summaries with id, name, description, and timestamps. Results are ordered consistently for stable display. Soft-deleted categories are excluded from results.

This operation is accessible to all authenticated users (customers, sellers, administrators) for category browsing purposes. Administrators use this to manage category structure, while customers and sellers use it for navigation and product organization.
operations.name: iterate
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_categories table filtering by parent_id equals the provided categoryId parameter. Return all direct child categories (subcategories) of the specified parent. Join not required as all needed data is in the categories table. Filter out soft-deleted categories (deleted_at is null). Order results by created_at or name for consistent display. Return empty array if no children exist. Validate categoryId is valid UUID format before query.

responseBody.description: Array of subcategory summaries belonging to the specified parent category. Empty array returned if no children exist.

parameters.description: UUID of the parent category to retrieve children for. Must reference an existing, non-deleted category.
parameters.name: categoryId

prerequisites.description: Parent category must be created before its children can be retrieved, as categoryId must reference an existing category

operations.description:
Create a new product category in the catalog.

This endpoint allows administrators to create new categories for organizing products. Categories can be created as top-level categories or as subcategories under existing parent categories, supporting exactly one level of nesting.

The category name must be unique across all categories. The description is optional and provides additional context about the category's contents. When creating a subcategory, the parentId field references an existing top-level category.

Only administrators can access this endpoint. Non-administrator requests are rejected with an authorization error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shopping_mall_categories record with the provided name, description, and optional parent_id.

1. Verify the authenticated user has administrator role authorization.
2. Validate that the category name is unique by checking against existing categories (including soft-deleted ones if applicable).
3. If parentId is provided, verify the parent category exists and is not deleted.
4. Enforce one-level nesting: if parentId is provided, verify the parent category itself has no parent (is a top-level category).
5. Generate a new UUID for the category id.
6. Insert the new category record with created_at and updated_at timestamps set to current time.
7. Return the complete created category entity.

Error handling:
- 403: Non-administrator user attempts to create category
- 400: Duplicate category name
- 400: Parent category does not exist or is deleted
- 400: Attempting to create subcategory under a subcategory (deep nesting)

responseBody.description: The newly created category entity with all fields including generated id and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Category creation data including name (required), optional description, and optional parentId for subcategories.

operations.description:
Update an existing category's name and description.

This endpoint allows administrators to modify category information including the display name and description text. The category must exist and be accessible. Only administrators can perform this operation - sellers and customers are rejected.

The name field must be unique across all categories. If the new name conflicts with an existing category, the request is rejected. The description is optional and can be set to null for simple categories.

Upon successful update, the complete category object is returned with updated timestamps. The updated_at field reflects when the modification occurred.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update shopping_mall_categories record by categoryId UUID.

Validate requester has administrator role - reject non-admin users.
Verify category exists and is not soft deleted.
Validate name uniqueness against all categories (check @@unique([name]) constraint).
Validate name is provided and not empty.
Update name and description fields from request body.
Set updated_at to current timestamp.
Return complete IShoppingMallCategory entity.

Handle errors: 404 if category not found, 409 if name conflict, 403 if not admin.

responseBody.description: Complete category entity with updated information and timestamps.

parameters.description: Category identifier (UUID format).
parameters.name: categoryId

requestBody.description: Category update data including name and optional description.

prerequisites.description: Category must be created before it can be updated - the categoryId path parameter must reference an existing category record

operations.description:
Delete a category from the catalog.

This operation removes a category from the platform. Only administrators can delete categories. When a category is deleted, all products previously assigned to that category become uncategorized but remain visible on the platform. If the deleted category is a parent category, all its subcategories are also deleted along with their products becoming uncategorized.

The deletion is implemented as a soft delete, marking the category with a deleted_at timestamp rather than permanently removing it from the database. This preserves audit trail and allows for potential recovery.

Attempting to delete a category as a non-administrator, seller, or customer will be rejected. The category must exist and not already be deleted.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the category with the given categoryId by setting its deleted_at timestamp to the current time.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user has administrator role (admin or superAdmin)
2. Query shopping_mall_categories table for the category with matching id
3. If category not found, return 404 Not Found
4. If category already deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404 Not Found
5. Set deleted_at to current timestamp and save
6. Cascade delete applies automatically to child subcategories via database relation (onDelete: Cascade)
7. Products referencing this category become uncategorized (category_id set to null via CASCADE or application logic)
8. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Non-administrator user: reject with 403 Forbidden
- Category not found: return 404 Not Found
- Category already deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Parent category deletion: cascade deletes all child subcategories

parameters.description: UUID of the category to delete (administrator access required).
parameters.name: categoryId

prerequisites.description: Category must be created before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Search and list products with pagination, filtering, and sorting capabilities.

This endpoint provides comprehensive product discovery functionality for customers and guests. Users can search products by name, filter by category, apply price range constraints, and filter by stock availability. Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page size.

The search supports full-text matching on product name and description fields. Category filtering includes products from the specified category and can optionally include subcategories. Price range filters accept minimum and maximum values. Stock filtering shows only products with at least one variant having positive inventory.

Sorting options include relevance (for text search), price (ascending or descending), newest (by created_at), and name (alphabetical). The default sort is by relevance when searching, or by newest when browsing without search terms.

Guest users can access this endpoint to browse the catalog. Results exclude products from suspended sellers and soft-deleted products.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_products table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters:
- name: Full-text search using gin_trgm_ops index on name and description columns
- shopping_mall_category_id: Filter by category, optionally include subcategories by joining children
- minPrice/maxPrice: Filter base_price within range
- inStock: Join with shopping_mall_product_variants and filter where stock_quantity > 0
- seller status: Join with shopping_mall_sellers and exclude where approval_status != 'approved' or deleted_at is set

Exclude soft-deleted products (deleted_at IS NULL).

Apply sorting based on sort parameter:
- 'relevance': Order by text search score (when name query provided)
- 'price_asc': ORDER BY base_price ASC
- 'price_desc': ORDER BY base_price DESC
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC
- 'name_asc': ORDER BY name ASC

Implement cursor-based or offset pagination. Return IPageIShoppingMallProduct.ISummary with product summary fields including id, name, base_price, category info, seller info, first image URL, and stock status.

Handle edge cases:
- Empty result set: Return page with empty items array
- Invalid category ID: Return 404
- Invalid price range (min > max): Return validation error
- Page size exceeds maximum: Cap at maximum allowed

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summary records optimized for catalog browsing and search result displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including product name query, category filter, price range, stock availability filter, sorting options, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Create a new product listing on the platform.

Sellers can create products by providing the product name, description, category assignment, and base price. The product is automatically associated with the authenticated seller who creates it and cannot be transferred to another seller.

The product name and description are required fields used for search and display purposes. The category must be a valid category or subcategory ID from the platform's category hierarchy. The base price represents the standard price before any variant-specific adjustments.

Upon successful creation, the product is visible in search results and category listings but marked as unavailable until at least one product variant is added. Products must have at least one variant to be purchasable by customers.

Sellers who are suspended by administrators cannot create products. Attempting to create a product while suspended results in rejection with an appropriate error message.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product record in the shopping_mall_products table.

1. Validate the authenticated user is a seller with active approval status (not suspended).
2. Validate the shopping_mall_category_id exists in shopping_mall_categories table.
3. Validate required fields: name (non-empty string), description (non-empty string), base_price (positive number).
4. Extract seller_id from the authenticated session context (do not accept from request body).
5. Insert new record with: id (UUID), shopping_mall_seller_id, shopping_mall_category_id, name, description, base_price, created_at (current timestamp), updated_at (current timestamp), deleted_at (null).
6. Return the created product record.

Error handling:
- Reject if seller account is suspended (403 Forbidden).
- Reject if category_id does not exist (404 Not Found).
- Reject if required fields are missing or invalid (400 Bad Request).
- Reject if base_price is zero or negative (400 Bad Request).

responseBody.description: The newly created product record with all fields populated including system-generated id, created_at, and updated_at timestamps.

requestBody.description: Product creation data including name, description, category assignment, and base price. The seller association is derived from authentication context.

prerequisites.description: Category must exist before a product can reference it via shopping_mall_category_id. Product creation validates the category ID exists and returns 404 Not Found if the category is not found.

operations.description:
Retrieves complete details of a single product by its unique identifier.

Returns the full product entity including name, description, base price, category assignment, and seller information. The response includes all product images in display order, with the first image serving as the main thumbnail. All product variants are included with their SKU codes, option value combinations, and optional price overrides.

Stock availability for each variant is calculated from the inventory records ledger. Products that are soft deleted (deleted_at is set) return 404 Not Found to hide them from customers while preserving order history references.

This endpoint is accessible to all actors including guests for product browsing. The product must exist and be active (not deleted) to be retrieved.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_products table by productId UUID. Join with shopping_mall_product_images to include all images ordered by display_order. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to include all variants with their option_values and prices. Calculate stock status from shopping_mall_inventory_records ledger for each variant. Return 404 if product not found or if deleted_at is not null (soft deleted products are hidden). Include seller profile information (shop_name, logo_image_url) from shopping_mall_seller_profiles. Include category information from shopping_mall_categories.

responseBody.description: Complete product entity including all images, variants, seller profile, and category information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Delete a product from the platform.

Sellers can delete their own products only when specific conditions are met: no pending order items in paid or shipped status for any variant, no pending cancellation requests, and no pending refund requests. When these conditions are satisfied, the product is soft deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp.

Administrators can delete any product on the platform for policy violations, bypassing the standard deletion conditions. This elevated permission enables platform oversight and content moderation.

Upon deletion, the product is immediately hidden from search results, category listings, and cannot be purchased. All product variants are also deleted. The product and its snapshots remain accessible for order history and dispute resolution. If the deleted product exists in customer wishlists, it is automatically removed from all wishlists.

Reject with 400 if any pending items exist. For admin requests, skip condition validation. Set deleted_at to current timestamp. Cascade delete all product_variants and their inventory_records. Remove product from all shopping_mall_wishlist_items. Return 204 No Content on success. Return 403 Forbidden if seller attempts to delete another seller's product. Return 404 Not Found if product does not exist.

Products from suspended sellers are excluded from results. Deleted products (soft-deleted with deleted_at set) are excluded by default but can be included using the status filter for sellers reviewing their deleted catalog.

Upload a new product image to a product's image gallery.

This endpoint allows sellers to add images to their products. Each product can have multiple images displayed in a gallery sequence. The display_order field determines the image position in the gallery, with lower values appearing first. The image with display_order 0 serves as the main thumbnail shown in product listings and search results.

Only the owning seller can upload images to their products. The image URL should point to a valid image file stored in the platform's object storage or CDN. After upload, sellers can reorder images or delete them as needed.

Validate the image URL format and ensure it points to an accessible resource. Check that display_order is a non-negative integer. If display_order conflicts with existing images, shift subsequent images to maintain consecutive ordering. Create the product image record with the provided url and display_order. Set created_at and updated_at timestamps automatically. Return the newly created product image entity with all fields including the generated id.

Reorder product images by updating their display order sequence.

This operation allows sellers to change the display sequence of images for their products. The display order determines how images appear in the product gallery, with the first image (display_order 0) serving as the main thumbnail shown in product listings and search results.

Sellers can only reorder images for products they own. The operation accepts an array of image IDs with their new display order values. Display orders should be consecutive integers starting from 0. After reordering, the new first image automatically becomes the main thumbnail.

The operation validates that all provided image IDs belong to the specified product and that the seller owns the product. If validation fails, the operation returns an error without making any changes.

Query shopping_mall_product_images table for all images belonging to the product.

Validate that all image IDs in the request body belong to this product.

Validate that display_order values are consecutive integers starting from 0.

Begin database transaction.

For each image in the request, update the display_order field with the new value.

Commit transaction.

Query and return all images for the product in the new order.

Error handling: Return 403 if seller doesn't own the product. Return 404 if product or any image ID doesn't exist. Return 400 if display_order values are invalid (not consecutive, duplicate values, or missing images).

operations.description:
Delete a product image from a product.

This endpoint allows sellers to remove individual images from their products. The image is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp, preserving the record for audit trail and snapshot history. If the deleted image was the main thumbnail (first in display order), the system automatically designates the next image in sequence as the new thumbnail.

Sellers can only delete images from products they own. The operation validates that the seller owns the product before proceeding. Deletion is blocked if the product has only one active image remaining, as at least one image must always be present on a product.

The deleted image information is preserved in product snapshots created at the time of deletion, maintaining historical records for dispute resolution and audit purposes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated seller owns the product by checking shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id matches the seller's ID.

2. Verify the image exists and belongs to the specified product by checking shopping_mall_product_images.shopping_mall_product_id matches productId.

3. Check that the image is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).

4. Count active images on the product. If only one active image exists, reject the deletion with an error indicating at least one image must remain.

5. If the deleted image has display_order 0 (main thumbnail), reorder remaining images so the next image becomes the new thumbnail.

6. Soft-delete the image by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.

7. Trigger creation of a product snapshot to capture the image deletion event, preserving the image state before deletion.

8. Return 204 No Content on success.

Query shopping_mall_product_variants table filtered by shopping_mall_product_id matching the path parameter.

Exclude soft-deleted variants (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results by default.

- sku_code: partial match using LIKE operator
- option_values: partial match using LIKE operator  
- min_price/max_price: range filter on price column
- in_stock: boolean filter calculating current stock from shopping_mall_inventory_records sum

Join with shopping_mall_inventory_records to calculate current stock quantity (SUM of quantity deltas).

Apply sorting based on request parameters (default: created_at DESC).

Return cursor-based pagination with IPageIShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary response type.

operations.description:
Create a new product variant for the specified product.

This endpoint allows sellers to add variants to their products. Each variant represents a specific combination of options (such as color, size, or other attributes) identified by a unique SKU code within the product context. Variants enable customers to select specific configurations when purchasing.

The variant's SKU code must be unique within the product but can be reused across different products. Option values provide a human-readable description of the variant configuration (e.g., 'Color: Red, Size: Large'). An optional price override can be specified; if null, the product's base price applies.

Sellers can only create variants for products they own. The seller's account must be in approved status (not suspended). Every variant creation is recorded for audit purposes. A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable by customers.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the authenticated user is a seller with approved status (not suspended). Query shopping_mall_products table to verify the product exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (shopping_mall_seller_id matches). Reject if product is deleted (deleted_at is not null). Validate request body: sku_code must be non-empty string, option_values must be non-empty string, price is optional number. Check uniqueness constraint: query shopping_mall_product_variants where shopping_mall_product_id equals productId and sku_code equals request sku_code. If exists, reject with conflict error. Insert new record into shopping_mall_product_variants with: id (UUID v4), shopping_mall_product_id (from path), sku_code, option_values, price (null if not provided), created_at and updated_at (current timestamp), deleted_at (null). Return the created variant entity. Note: Variant snapshots are created on edit operations, not on initial creation.

responseBody.description: The newly created product variant entity with all fields including system-generated id and timestamps.

The variant's price field may be null, indicating the product's base price applies. Stock quantities are not stored in this table - they are calculated from the inventory records ledger.

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant with new SKU code, option values, and optional price override.

This endpoint allows sellers to modify their product variant details. Sellers can update the SKU code, option values text representation, and price override. The price field is optional - when null, the product's base price applies to this variant.

Every variant edit automatically creates an immutable snapshot preserving the previous state for audit trail and dispute resolution. The snapshot includes all variant fields at the moment of edit.

Sellers can only update variants belonging to their own products. Attempts to update variants from other sellers' products are rejected. Suspended sellers cannot perform this operation - all their product operations are blocked.

The variant must not be soft-deleted. Updating a deleted variant returns an error. If there are pending order items or cancellation/refund requests for this variant, the update may still proceed as these constraints apply to deletion, not updates.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Verify the authenticated user is a seller with active (non-suspended) status.
2. Validate productId is a valid UUID format.
3. Validate variantId is a valid UUID format.
4. Query shopping_mall_products table to verify product exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (shopping_mall_seller_id matches).
5. If product not found or seller mismatch, return 404 Not Found.
6. Query shopping_mall_product_variants table to find variant by id where shopping_mall_product_id = productId and deleted_at IS NULL.
7. If variant not found, return 404 Not Found.
8. Validate request body: sku_code must be non-empty string, option_values must be non-empty string, price is optional (number or null).
9. Check sku_code uniqueness within the product: query for existing variant with same shopping_mall_product_id and sku_code where id != variantId and deleted_at IS NULL. If exists, return 409 Conflict.
10. Begin database transaction.
11. Create snapshot record in shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots table with current variant state (all fields before update).
12. Update shopping_mall_product_variants: set sku_code, option_values, price, and updated_at to current timestamp.
13. Commit transaction.
14. Return updated variant entity with all fields including id, shopping_mall_product_id, sku_code, option_values, price, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

responseBody.description: The updated product variant entity with all fields reflecting the new values and updated timestamp.

parameters.name: productId

parameters.description: UUID of the variant to update.
parameters.name: variantId

requestBody.description: Variant update data including SKU code, option values, and optional price override. All fields are required except price which can be null to use product base price.

Variant must be created before it can be updated

operations.description:
Delete a product variant by removing it from the product's variant list.

This operation allows sellers to delete variants from their own products. The variant is soft-deleted (marked with deleted_at timestamp) rather than permanently removed, preserving references in historical orders and snapshots.

Deletion is only permitted when the variant has no pending order items in paid or shipped status, and no pending cancellation or refund requests. If any of these conditions exist, the deletion request is rejected to protect existing customer orders and pending requests.

When a variant is deleted, all associated inventory records are also soft-deleted through cascade deletion. The variant and its inventory records are immediately hidden from search results, product listings, and cart operations. Customers cannot add deleted variants to their cart or purchase them.

This endpoint requires seller authentication and ownership verification - sellers can only delete variants from their own products. Administrators cannot delete variants through this endpoint; they must delete the entire product if necessary for policy violations.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting user as a seller.
2. Verify the seller owns the product by checking shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID.
3. Verify the variant exists and belongs to the specified product by checking shopping_mall_product_variants.shopping_mall_product_id equals productId.
4. Check if the variant is already deleted (deleted_at is not null) - if so, return 404.
5. Validate deletion constraints:
   - Query shopping_mall_order_items for any records with this variant_id where status is 'paid' or 'shipped' and deleted_at is null. If found, reject with 400.
   - Query shopping_mall_cancellation_requests for any records linked to order items of this variant where status is 'pending' and deleted_at is null. If found, reject with 400.
   - Query shopping_mall_refund_requests for any records linked to order items of this variant where status is 'pending' and deleted_at is null. If found, reject with 400.
6. If all validations pass, perform soft delete:
   - Update shopping_mall_product_variants set deleted_at = current timestamp where id = variantId.
   - Cascade delete is handled by database trigger or application logic to soft-delete related shopping_mall_inventory_records.
7. Return 204 No Content on success.

Edge cases:
- Product not found or not owned by seller: 404
- Variant not found or already deleted: 404
- Pending order items exist: 400 with error message
- Pending cancellation/refund requests exist: 400 with error message
- Variant is the last variant of the product: Allow deletion (product becomes unavailable for purchase but remains visible)

operations.description:
Retrieve historical snapshots of a specific product.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of product snapshots, which are immutable audit records capturing the complete product state at the time of each edit. Each snapshot preserves the product's name, description, category, and base price as they existed when the edit occurred.

Sellers can view snapshots of their own products only. Administrators can view snapshots of any product on the platform for oversight purposes. This endpoint supports filtering by creation date range and pagination for efficient browsing of product change history.

Snapshots are created automatically when products are edited and cannot be modified or deleted. The snapshots are ordered chronologically with the most recent changes first.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_product_snapshots table filtered by shopping_mall_product_id.

Authorization: Verify requester is either (1) the seller who owns the product, or (2) an administrator. Reject customers and unauthorized sellers.

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based pagination from request body. Support date range filtering on created_at field. Order results by created_at DESC (newest first).

Join with shopping_mall_products to verify ownership (for seller authorization). Include snapshot fields: id, shopping_mall_category_id, name, description, base_price, created_at.

Return IPageIShoppingMallProductSnapshot.ISummary with pagination metadata (page, limit, total count).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product snapshot summary records showing historical product states.

parameters.description: Product ID (UUID format) identifying the product whose snapshots to retrieve.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Search criteria including pagination parameters and optional date range filters for created_at.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific product snapshot by ID.

This endpoint returns the complete snapshot record capturing the product state at a specific point in time. Each snapshot preserves the denormalized product fields (name, description, category, base price) when a product was edited, enabling historical tracking and dispute resolution.

Sellers can view snapshots of their own products only. Administrators can view snapshots of any product on the platform for oversight purposes. The snapshot includes all captured fields and references to nested variant snapshots.

Returns 403 Forbidden if a seller attempts to access a snapshot for a product they do not own. Returns 404 Not Found if the snapshot ID does not exist or the product ID does not match the snapshot's product reference.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_product_snapshots table by snapshot ID. Verify the snapshot exists and the productId parameter matches the shopping_mall_product_id foreign key. Perform authorization check: if actor is seller, verify they own the product (shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id matches authenticated seller); if actor is admin, allow access to any snapshot. Join with shopping_mall_categories to include category details if needed. Return the complete snapshot record including id, product reference, category reference, name, description, base_price, and created_at. This endpoint allows sellers to view all variants associated with a product, supporting pagination for products with many variants. Variants can be filtered by SKU code or option values. The operation returns variant summaries including SKU, option values, price, and stock status calculated from inventory records.

Variants are subsidiary entities that belong to a parent product and cannot exist independently. Only the product owner (seller) can access this endpoint for their products. Administrators can access variants of any product for oversight purposes.

Create a new product variant for a specific product.

Sellers use this endpoint to add variants representing specific SKU combinations (such as color, size, or other option combinations) to their products. Each variant requires a unique SKU code within the product context and human-readable option values for display in cart, orders, and product listings.

The variant's price is optional - when not provided, the product's base price applies. Initial stock quantity starts at zero and must be added through the inventory restock endpoint. A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable by customers.

The requesting seller must own the product referenced in the request. Duplicate SKU codes within the same product are rejected.

Every variant update creates an immutable snapshot to preserve the previous state for audit trail purposes. The snapshot captures all variant fields at the moment of edit.

Sellers can only update variants belonging to their own products. Attempting to update a variant from another seller's product will be rejected. Variants with pending order items or active cancellation/refund requests may have update restrictions to prevent disruption to customer orders.

Retrieve the authenticated customer's shopping cart with all cart items.

Returns the customer's personal shopping cart containing all items they have added for potential purchase. Each cart item includes the product variant details, quantity, and pricing information. The cart belongs exclusively to the authenticated customer and cannot be accessed by other users.

The response includes the cart metadata (creation and update timestamps) and all cart items with their associated product variant information. Cart total price is calculated dynamically from the cart items and is not stored in the database.

Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to get variant details including option values. Join with shopping_mall_products to get product names and descriptions. Return the cart entity with nested items array. If cart doesn't exist, return null or create empty cart. Handle soft-deleted carts appropriately.

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the customer's shopping cart.

This endpoint allows customers to add items to their shopping cart by specifying a product variant and quantity. If the same variant already exists in the cart, the quantity is combined with the existing amount rather than creating a duplicate entry, enforced by the unique constraint on cart and product variant.

The cart is automatically determined from the authenticated customer's session, as each customer has exactly one active cart. The operation returns the created or updated cart item with the final quantity.

Customers can add available product variants to their cart for later purchase during checkout. Unavailable variants may be added but will block checkout until removed.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create or update a cart item for the authenticated customer's cart.

1. Retrieve the authenticated customer's cart from session (shopping_mall_carts where member_id = current user and deleted_at IS NULL)
2. Check if cart item already exists for the given product variant (unique constraint on shopping_mall_cart_id, shopping_mall_product_variant_id)
3. If exists: UPDATE the quantity by adding the new quantity to existing quantity
4. If not exists: INSERT new cart item with the specified quantity
5. Return the cart item with final quantity
6. Validate product variant exists and is active before adding
7. Validate quantity is positive integer (minimum 1)

Edge cases:
- If variant is out of stock, still allow adding but mark as unavailable in cart view
- If quantity exceeds available stock, allow adding but checkout will be blocked
- Cart is created automatically if customer doesn't have one yet

responseBody.description: The created or updated cart item with the final quantity after combining with existing items.

requestBody.description: Product variant identifier and quantity to add to the cart. Quantity must be a positive integer. If the variant already exists in the cart, the quantity will be combined with the existing amount.

prerequisites.description: Product variant must be created by a seller before customers can add it to their shopping cart. The variant must exist with a valid ID, SKU code, and option values.

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a specific cart item.

This endpoint allows customers to modify the quantity of a product variant in their shopping cart. The cart item must exist and belong to the authenticated customer. Quantity can be increased or decreased based on product availability.

The operation validates that the requested quantity is positive and does not exceed available stock. If the quantity is set to zero or below, the item should be removed from the cart instead.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_cart_items by cartItemId UUID. Verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer through the cart's member_id relationship. Validate the new quantity is a positive integer. Check product variant availability and stock levels. Update the quantity field and updated_at timestamp. Return the complete updated cart item with product variant details joined if needed for response.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item with the new quantity and current timestamps.

parameters.description: Cart item UUID (global scope)
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: Update request containing the new quantity for the cart item.

prerequisites.description: Cart item must be created before it can be updated. The cart item is identified by cartItemId in the path parameter and must exist in the system.

operations.description:
Remove a specific item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation permanently deletes the specified cart item from the customer's cart. The removal is immediate and cannot be undone. After deletion, the cart total price is automatically recalculated to reflect the removed item.

Customers can remove any item from their cart at any time before order placement, including both available and unavailable items. This operation is commonly used when customers decide they no longer want to purchase a specific item or need to remove unavailable items before checkout.

The cart item is identified by its unique cartItemId. Only the cart owner (authenticated customer) can delete items from their own cart. Attempting to delete another customer's cart item will result in an authorization error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the cart item record from shopping_mall_cart_items table by cartItemId.

1. Verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer
2. Delete the cart item record from shopping_mall_cart_items table
3. Recalculate the parent cart's total price by summing remaining cart items
4. Return success response (204 No Content or null response body)

Business rules:
- Customer can only delete items from their own cart
- Deletion is immediate and permanent (not reversible)
- Cart total must be recalculated after deletion
- Works for both available and unavailable items
- If cart becomes empty, cart remains but with zero items

Edge cases:
- Cart item already deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Cart item belongs to different customer: return 403 Forbidden
- Cart item does not exist: return 404 Not Found

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item to remove (UUID format, scoped to customer's cart)
parameters.name: cartItemId

prerequisites.description: Cart item must be created before it can be deleted. This operation creates the cart item record in shopping_mall_cart_items that the DELETE operation will remove.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of customer orders with filtering and sorting capabilities.

This endpoint allows customers to browse their order history with flexible search criteria. Orders are sorted by creation date (newest first) by default. Customers can filter orders by status, date ranges, and search by order code.

The operation returns order summaries optimized for list display, including order code, total price, status, and item count. Full order details with items and shipments are available through the GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

Authentication required: Only the authenticated customer's orders are returned. Administrators have separate oversight endpoints for viewing all platform orders.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table filtered by the authenticated member's member_id. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach. Support filtering by: status (exact match or array), created_at date range (gte/lte), order code search (partial match). Support sorting by created_at (asc/desc), total_price (asc/desc). Default sort: created_at DESC. Join with shopping_mall_order_items to compute item count per order. Exclude soft-deleted orders (deleted_at IS NULL). Return IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary with pagination metadata (page, limit, total count, hasMore). Handle empty result sets gracefully. Validate date range formats. Reject invalid status values.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summary records for the authenticated customer, including pagination metadata for navigation.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status filters, order code search, date range filters, pagination parameters (page, limit), and sorting options (field, direction).

operations.description:
Retrieves the complete details of a specific order including order items, product snapshots, and shipment tracking information.

This endpoint returns a single order with all its constituent data: order metadata (code, total price, timestamps), the list of order items with product details and variant options, associated shipments with carrier and tracking information, and the shipping address used for the order.

Customers can only access their own orders. The order items include snapshot data preserving the product name, description, variant price, and seller shop information at the time of purchase. Each shipment shows tracking number, carrier name, and delivery status.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table by UUID primary key. Verify the authenticated customer's member_id matches the order's member_id for authorization. Eager load related shopping_mall_order_items with their shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots and shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options. Include shopping_mall_shipments with carrier and tracking details. Join with shopping_mall_customer_addresses to include the shipping address snapshot if available. Return 404 if order not found or access denied. Do not include soft-deleted orders unless explicitly requested for admin oversight.

responseBody.description: Complete order details including order metadata, order items with product snapshots, shipments with tracking information, and shipping address.

parameters.description: Order UUID identifier (primary key).
parameters.name: orderId

operations.description:
Place a new order by processing the customer's shopping cart items into a permanent order record.

This endpoint creates a complete order transaction, capturing all cart items with their product details, prices, and quantities at the time of purchase. The system generates a unique order code for customer reference and calculates the total order value. Each order item is linked to its product, variant, and seller for fulfillment tracking.

Upon successful order creation, the customer's cart items are removed, inventory records are created to deduct stock quantities, and the order enters the 'paid' status awaiting seller shipment. The operation is atomic - if any step fails (payment, inventory deduction, order item creation), the entire transaction is rolled back.

The returned order object includes all order items with their initial 'paid' status. Shipments are created later by sellers when they fulfill the order items.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new order for the authenticated customer through the following steps:

1. Validate the customer's cart exists and contains at least one item
2. Retrieve all cart items with their associated product variants
3. Validate all variants are available (not deleted, have sufficient stock)
4. Calculate total price from cart items (quantity × variant price or product base price)
5. Generate unique order code (format: date-based + sequence)
6. Create shopping_mall_orders record with member_id, code, total_price, timestamps
7. For each cart item, create shopping_mall_order_items record with:
   - shopping_mall_order_id (new order)
   - shopping_mall_product_id
   - shopping_mall_product_variant_id
   - shopping_mall_seller_id (from variant's product)
   - quantity, price (snapshot at purchase time)
   - status: 'paid'
   - timestamps
8. Create inventory records for each variant to deduct stock quantities
9. Remove all cart items from the customer's cart
10. Return the complete order object with all order items

Use database transaction to ensure atomicity. If any step fails, rollback entire operation. Return appropriate error responses for insufficient stock, deleted variants, or payment failures.

responseBody.description: Complete order object including all order items with their initial 'paid' status, order code for customer reference, and total price snapshot.

requestBody.description: Order creation request containing shipping address reference and optional payment method information. The cart items are automatically converted to order items - no need to specify them explicitly as they come from the customer's active cart.

prerequisites.description: Customer must have at least one saved shipping address before placing an order, as the order creation request requires a valid shopping_mall_customer_address_id reference
Customer must have items in their shopping cart before checkout, as orders are created by converting cart items to order items and the system validates cart contains at least one item

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all orders on the platform with search and filtering capabilities.

This endpoint allows administrators to view and search across all customer orders regardless of ownership. Administrators can filter orders by customer, seller, order status, date ranges, and search by order code. The response includes order summary information optimized for administrative oversight dashboards.

Administrators use this endpoint to monitor platform activity, investigate specific orders, and identify orders requiring intervention such as force-cancellation or force-refund operations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table with pagination and filtering. Join with shopping_mall_members for customer information and shopping_mall_order_items for seller and status aggregation. Apply search filters on order code, member_id, seller_id, status, and created_at date ranges. Support sorting by created_at (newest first by default), code, or total_price. Return cursor-based pagination with IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary response type. Exclude soft-deleted orders (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results. Include order item count and current aggregated status in summary.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summary records for administrative oversight, including order code, customer information, total price, status, and item count.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including order code partial match, customer ID, seller ID, order status filter, date range filters, pagination parameters (page, limit), and sorting options.

operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific order by its ID.

Administrators can access any order on the platform regardless of customer or seller ownership. This endpoint returns the full order details including order number, total price, creation timestamp, and all associated order items with their product snapshots and shipment information.

The response includes order items with product name, variant options, quantity, price, and item status. Each order item includes its snapshot preserving the product state at purchase time. Shipments are included with carrier name, tracking number, and delivery timestamps.

This endpoint is restricted to administrator and super administrator roles. Regular customers can only access their own orders through a different endpoint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table by primary key ID. Verify the requesting user has administrator or super_admin role. Eagerly load related order items with their snapshots and snapshot options. Include shipments with their associated order items. Return 404 if order not found or if order is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null). Join with shopping_mall_members for customer information if needed. Include product snapshot data from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots and shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options tables.

responseBody.description: Complete order details including order metadata, all order items with product snapshots, and shipment tracking information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the order to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: orderId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order items within a specific order.

This endpoint returns all items belonging to the specified order, with optional filtering by fulfillment status. Each order item represents a specific product variant purchased, including quantity, unit price, and current status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded).

The response includes product details, variant options, seller information, and shipment tracking data when available. Results are paginated to handle orders with many items efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_order_items table filtered by shopping_mall_order_id matching the orderId path parameter. Apply optional status filter from request body. Join with shopping_mall_products for product name, shopping_mall_product_variants for variant options, and shopping_mall_sellers for seller information. Include shipment tracking info if shopping_mall_shipment_id is not null. Apply pagination with cursor or offset-based approach. Return summary DTOs optimized for list display. Order results by created_at descending.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summary records with product details, variant options, seller information, and shipment tracking data.

parameters.description: UUID of the order to retrieve items from (scoped to authenticated customer's orders).
parameters.name: orderId

requestBody.description: Search criteria including optional status filter and pagination parameters for controlling result set size and navigation.

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before its items can be retrieved. Order items are created atomically with the order during checkout and cannot exist without a parent order.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information for a specific order item within its parent order.

This endpoint returns complete order item details including product information, variant options, quantity, unit price, and current fulfillment status. The order item is scoped to its parent order for access validation.

Customers can view their own order items. Sellers can view order items for products they sell. Administrators can view any order item on the platform. The response includes product name, variant configuration, seller information, shipment tracking (if shipped), and item status for tracking fulfillment progress.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_items table by id with parent order validation.

1. Validate orderItemId exists in shopping_mall_order_items table
2. Verify the item's shopping_mall_order_id matches the provided orderId (scope validation)
3. Join with shopping_mall_products for product name and details
4. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants for variant option values
5. Join with shopping_mall_sellers for seller profile information
6. Left join with shopping_mall_shipments for tracking information if shopping_mall_shipment_id is not null
7. Check authorization: requester must be the order's member_id, the item's seller_id, or an administrator
8. Return full IShoppingMallOrderItem with all related data

Edge cases:
- Order item not found: return 404
- OrderId doesn't match item's order: return 404 (don't reveal item exists under different order)
- Unauthorized access: return 403

responseBody.description: Complete order item details including product information, variant options, quantity, price, fulfillment status, and shipment tracking if available.

parameters.description: Parent order ID (UUID format) - used for scope validation to ensure the order item belongs to this order.
parameters.name: orderId

parameters.description: Order item ID (UUID format) - uniquely identifies the specific order item to retrieve.
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of order items belonging to the authenticated seller.

This endpoint enables sellers to view and manage their order items through their dashboard. Sellers can filter items by fulfillment status to focus on pending actions such as items awaiting shipment (paid), items in transit (shipped), or items requiring attention (cancelled, refunded). The operation supports date range filtering to query orders from specific time periods.

Each order item in the response includes essential information for fulfillment: the order code for customer reference, product details, variant options, quantity, unit price, current status, and shipment tracking information when available. Items are sorted by creation date with newest orders appearing first.

The seller context is automatically determined from the authentication session - sellers can only access their own order items. This endpoint is essential for seller order management workflows including preparing shipments, responding to cancellation requests, and processing refunds.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_order_items table filtered by the authenticated seller's ID from session context. Apply status filter if provided in request body (allowed values: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded). Support date range filtering on created_at for order history queries. Implement cursor-based or offset pagination with limit and page parameters. Join with shopping_mall_orders to include order code for customer reference. Join with shopping_mall_products for product name. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants for option_values and SKU. Join with shopping_mall_shipments for tracking information when shipped_at is present. Sort by created_at descending (newest first) by default. Return summary fields optimized for seller dashboard display: item ID, order code, product name, variant options, quantity, price, status, shipment tracking info, and timestamps. Handle case where seller has no order items (empty array with pagination metadata).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summary records with fulfillment status, product details, and shipment tracking information for seller dashboard display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering seller's order items including status filter, date range, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item for the seller's products.

This endpoint returns complete order item details including the associated order, product, variant, quantity, price, current fulfillment status, and shipment information if assigned. Sellers use this to view order item details for fulfillment operations such as shipping, tracking, and customer service.

The order item must belong to the authenticated seller. If the order item belongs to a different seller, the request is rejected with an authorization error. This ensures sellers can only access and process their own order items within multi-seller orders.

The response includes the order item snapshot reference which preserves the product name, description, variant price, and seller shop information at the time of purchase for dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_order_items table by the provided orderItemId UUID.

Verify that the shopping_mall_seller_id on the order item matches the authenticated seller's ID. If not matched, reject with 403 Forbidden error indicating the seller does not own this order item.

Join with shopping_mall_orders to include order code and member information.
Join with shopping_mall_products to include product name and details.
Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to include SKU code and option values.
Left join with shopping_mall_shipments to include tracking information if shipment is assigned.
Include reference to the order item snapshot (shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots) which contains denormalized product and seller profile data at purchase time.

Return the complete order item entity with all related data. Handle the case where shipment_id is null (item not yet shipped) by returning null for shipment fields.

responseBody.description: Complete order item details including product, variant, quantity, price, status, and optional shipment information for seller fulfillment operations.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the order item to retrieve (UUID format, scoped to seller's products).
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve the snapshot of a specific order item showing the product name, description, variant price, and seller profile information as they appeared at the time of purchase.

This endpoint provides read-only access to the immutable order item snapshot, which preserves the exact state of the product and seller profile when the order was placed. This ensures accurate order history even if the original product has been modified or deleted, or if the seller has changed their shop name or logo.

Customers can access snapshots for their own order items through their order history. Sellers can view snapshots for order items containing their products. Administrators can view any order item snapshot on the platform for dispute resolution and oversight purposes.

The snapshot includes the product name, product description, variant price paid, seller shop name, and seller logo URL as they existed at purchase time. This endpoint is essential for customer order history viewing, seller order fulfillment reference, and administrative dispute resolution.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table by joining with shopping_mall_order_items to verify the orderId matches the orderItemId.

First, verify the orderItemId belongs to the specified orderId by checking shopping_mall_order_items where id = orderItemId AND shopping_mall_order_id = orderId. If no match, return 404.

Then retrieve the snapshot from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots where shopping_mall_order_item_id = orderItemId.

Apply authorization checks:
- Customer (member): Verify the order's member_id matches the authenticated customer's ID
- Seller: Verify the order item's shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
- Admin/Super Admin: Allow access to any snapshot

Return the full snapshot record including product_name, product_description, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_logo_url, and created_at.

If no snapshot exists for the order item (should not happen in normal operation), return 404.

responseBody.description: Complete order item snapshot record containing the preserved product and seller information at the time of purchase, including product name, description, variant price, seller shop name, and seller logo URL.

parameters.description: UUID of the parent order containing this order item (used for authorization and verification scope).
parameters.name: orderId

parameters.description: UUID of the order item whose snapshot is being retrieved.
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve variant option key-value pairs for a specific order item snapshot.

This endpoint returns the captured product variant options (such as color, size, material) exactly as they appeared at the time of purchase. Each option is represented as a key-value pair, where the key identifies the option type (e.g., 'color', 'size') and the value contains the selected option value (e.g., 'Red', 'Large').

The options are immutable historical records preserved in the order item snapshot. They remain accessible even if the original product or variant has been modified or deleted, ensuring accurate order history for customers and dispute resolution support for administrators.

Customers can view options for their own order items. Sellers can view options for order items containing their products. Administrators can view options for any order item on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options table filtered by the order item snapshot ID.

First, verify the order item exists and belongs to the specified order by joining shopping_mall_order_items with shopping_mall_orders.

Then, retrieve the snapshot record from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots using the unique shopping_mall_order_item_id foreign key.

Finally, fetch all option records from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options where shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_id matches the snapshot ID.

Return options as an array of key-value pair objects. Apply authorization checks: customers can only access their own orders, sellers can access order items with their products, administrators have full access.

Return 404 if order, order item, or snapshot does not exist. Return 403 if user lacks permission to access the order item.

responseBody.description: Array of variant option key-value pairs captured at purchase time, representing the complete variant configuration for the order item.

parameters.description: Order ID (UUID format, global scope)
parameters.name: orderId

parameters.description: Order item ID (UUID format, scoped to order)
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieves the order item snapshot for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns the immutable snapshot capturing the product name, description, variant price, and seller profile information as they existed at the time of purchase. The snapshot ensures order history accuracy even if the original product or seller profile has been modified or deleted since the order was placed.

The snapshot includes variant option values (e.g., color, size) stored as key-value pairs in the nested options array. All data is read-only and cannot be modified.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table by orderItemId parameter.

Join with shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options to include all variant option key-value pairs.

Verify caller has access to the order item:
- Customer: must own the parent order
- Seller: must be the seller of the order item
- Admin/SuperAdmin: unrestricted access

Return 404 if snapshot not found (order item may not have been purchased yet or was created before snapshot system).

Return complete snapshot object including:
- id, shopping_mall_order_item_id
- product_name, product_description
- variant_price
- seller_shop_name, seller_logo_url
- created_at
- options array with key-value pairs

responseBody.description: Complete order item snapshot record preserving product and seller state at purchase time, including variant option values.

parameters.description: Order item identifier (UUID format) to retrieve the snapshot for.
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve variant option key-value pairs for an order item snapshot.

This endpoint returns the captured variant configuration (option name and value pairs such as color: Red, size: Large) that was preserved at the time of purchase. Each order item snapshot contains multiple option records representing the complete variant specification the customer selected.

Sellers can access this information to understand exactly which product variant was purchased, supporting order fulfillment, inventory management, and dispute resolution. The options are immutable historical records that remain unchanged even if the original product variant is later modified or deleted.

The response includes all option key-value pairs associated with the order item snapshot, providing complete visibility into the purchased variant configuration.
operations.name: iterate
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options table by joining through shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots.

1. Validate orderItemId exists and belongs to a product sold by the authenticated seller
2. Find the snapshot record via shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots where shopping_mall_order_item_id = orderItemId
3. Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options where shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_id matches the snapshot
4. Return all option records with key-value pairs
5. Handle case where snapshot or options don't exist (404)
6. Enforce seller authorization: only allow access to order items containing their products

Edge cases: order item without snapshot (should not happen normally), order item with no variant options (return empty array).

responseBody.description: List of variant option key-value pairs captured at purchase time, showing the complete variant configuration the customer selected.

parameters.description: UUID of the order item to retrieve snapshot options for (scoped to seller's products).
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order item snapshots for administrative oversight and dispute resolution.

This endpoint allows administrators to browse the complete history of order item snapshots across the entire platform. Each snapshot preserves the exact state of a product and seller profile at the time of purchase, enabling accurate dispute resolution and audit trails.

Administrators can filter snapshots by product name, seller shop name, and creation date range. Results support sorting by timestamp, product name, or seller name. The response includes pagination metadata for navigating large result sets.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular members and sellers cannot access this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table with pagination and filtering. Apply search filters on product_name, seller_shop_name, created_at date range. Join with shopping_mall_order_items and shopping_mall_orders if order context filtering is requested. Support sorting by created_at (default descending), product_name, seller_shop_name. Return cursor-based or offset pagination for large result sets. Filter results to only include snapshots accessible by the administrator (all snapshots platform-wide). Handle edge case where snapshot has null seller_logo_url. Ensure query performance with proper indexing on created_at and foreign keys.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item snapshot summaries containing product name, seller shop name, variant price, and creation timestamp for administrative review.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including product name filter, seller shop name filter, creation date range, pagination parameters (page, limit), and sorting options (field and direction).

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information of a specific order item snapshot.

This endpoint returns the complete snapshot record preserving the product name, description, variant price, and seller profile information at the time of purchase. Order item snapshots are immutable audit records created automatically when orders are placed, ensuring accurate historical data for dispute resolution and order history display.

Administrators can access any order item snapshot on the platform regardless of customer or seller ownership. This enables oversight and investigation of order-related disputes or compliance reviews.

The snapshot includes denormalized product and seller data that remains unchanged even if the original product or seller profile is later modified or deleted. Variant option values are stored in a separate child table and can be accessed through related endpoints.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table by snapshot ID.

1. Validate snapshotId is a valid UUID format
2. Query the snapshot record where id = snapshotId
3. Return the full snapshot entity including all fields: id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, product_name, product_description, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_logo_url, created_at
4. Handle 404 error if snapshot ID does not exist
5. No authorization check needed beyond admin authentication (admins can view all snapshots per requirements)

No joins required as this returns the snapshot entity directly. The snapshot is immutable and read-only.

responseBody.description: Complete order item snapshot record preserving product and seller state at the time of purchase, including product name, description, variant price, seller shop name, and logo URL.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the order item snapshot (UUID format).
parameters.name: snapshotId

operations.description:
Retrieve all variant option key-value pairs for a specific order item snapshot.

This endpoint returns the complete set of option configurations (such as color, size, material) that were captured at the time of purchase. Each option is represented as a key-value pair stored in normalized format for efficient querying.

Administrators can access this endpoint for dispute resolution and order oversight purposes. The options reflect the exact variant configuration the customer selected when placing the order, preserved immutably even if the original product variant has been modified or deleted.

The snapshot and its options serve as the authoritative record of what variant configuration was purchased, supporting accurate order history and conflict resolution.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options table filtering by shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_id parameter.

1. Validate snapshotId exists in shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table
2. Verify requesting user has administrator privileges
3. Query all option records where shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_id matches the path parameter
4. Return array of options with id, key, value, and created_at fields
5. Order results by key for consistent response ordering

Edge cases:
- Return empty array if snapshot exists but has no options (simple product without variants)
- Return 404 if snapshotId does not exist
- Return 403 if user lacks administrator privileges

No pagination needed as option count per snapshot is typically small (2-5 options maximum).

responseBody.description: Array of variant option key-value pairs captured at purchase time, representing the complete option configuration of the purchased product variant.

parameters.description: UUID of the order item snapshot to retrieve options for (scoped to administrator oversight).
parameters.name: snapshotId

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of shipments associated with a specific order.

This endpoint returns all shipments created for the given order. Each shipment contains tracking information including carrier name and tracking number, along with timestamps for shipping and delivery events. Multiple shipments may exist for a single order when items come from different sellers, as each seller creates separate shipments.

The response includes shipment status derived from shipped_at and delivered_at timestamps. Shipments without delivered_at are considered in-transit. Customers can use this to track their order fulfillment progress. Sellers can view shipments they have created. Administrators have oversight access to all shipments.

Results are paginated and sorted by creation date (newest first). Filter criteria can be applied via the request body to narrow results by status, date range, or seller.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_shipments table filtered by shopping_mall_order_id matching the orderId path parameter. Join with shopping_mall_sellers to include seller information in response. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach. operations.description:
